To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TRPC1 contributes to SOCE-mediated Ca2+ signalling in the regulation of Ca2+ sensitive ACs.
TRPC1 is an integral part of the Ca2+-sensing machinery in HEK-AC8 and HSG cells and that this contributes to the dynamic inter-relationship between Ca2+ signalling and AC activity.
TRPC1 is required for STIM1- and Orai1-mediated Ca2+ influx and that it contributes to the Ca(2+)-dependent regulation of adenine nucleotide cyclases in HEK-AC8 cells and HSG cells.

a novel mechanism by which TRPC1 and STIM1 interact to influence Ca2+-dependent cAMP production.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SOCE is mediated via specific channels in the plasma membrane in response to ER Ca2+ depletion.
TRPC1 is an essential component of SOCE and contributes to the regulation of Ca2+ and Ca2+-sensing adenylate cyclises in HEK-AC8 and HSG cells.
TRPC1 and Orai channels act in tandem with STIM1 to form the SOCE complex that regulates ACs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TRPC1 is required for SOCE to occur, which is necessary for the Ca2+ and hence cAMP regulation of adenylates cyclases.
TRPC1 is a key component of SOCE in regulating cAMP production via AC8 and AC6.
TRPC1 is required for the regulation of AC8 activity by SOCE, but not for AC8 activation by Ca2+/calmodulin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TRPC1 is a key component of SOCE in HEK-AC8 and HSG cells, and its contribution to Ca2+ entry and AC regulation is independent of its role in Ca2+ signalling.
, in addition to STIM1 and TRPC1, Orai1 is a key component of SOCE in HEK-AC8 and HSG cells.
TRPC1 contributes to SOCE in a similar way to STIM1 and that TRPC1 is required for the regulation of AC8 and AC6 activity by cAMP.
